text:
opsbot: :rotating_light: Pager alert (P1) — automated detection: sudden per-org QPS spike for org LUMENBAY (org_id:LUM-522). 90% error-rate on /v1/generate for 3m, latency > 6s.

maya: paging in — I’m on it, grabbing logs now. Which services are showing the errors?

liam: seeing 503s from the rate-limiter service and a lot of downstream timeouts hitting the GPU pool. QPS to LUM-522 jumped x35 in 30s.

harper: support already has LumenBay on live-chat; customer says they started a bulk export job around 16:03 UTC. They’re seeing failed calls and 429s on their side.

maya: thanks. First priority: stop customer blast to restore platform stability. Can we apply emergency org throttle and disable non-essential heavy endpoints (batch-embed, async-batching) for LUM-522?

liam: agreed. Proposing temporary cap to 30 rps and a token-burst=60 while we investigate. Command I’ll run:

```
# CLI (run from ops jumpbox)
rictl org update --org-id LUM-522 --qps 30 --burst 60 --note "emergency mitigation 2019"
```

maya: go ahead. Also add exclusion for our monitoring probes to avoid masking.

liam: executing now.

opsbot: Command executed by liam at 2026-03-15T16:06:20Z: `rictl org update --org-id LUM-522 --qps 30 --burst 60 --note "emergency mitigation 2019"`

opsbot: Policy change applied (policy_id:emerg-LUM-522-2019). New effective QPS 30/60 burst.

harper: customer chat — they confirm requests dropped from >200 rps to ~28 rps. Their success rate improved but backlog of queued jobs persists.

maya: good. Next disable batch-embedding endpoint for that org to reduce long-running GPU calls. Command: 

```
# feature-flag toggle
rictl feature toggle --org LUM-522 --feature batch-embeddings --off --reason "emergency - heavy endpoint"
```

liam: toggled. opsbot: confirm?

opsbot: Feature toggle executed by liam at 2026-03-15T16:07:05Z: `batch-embeddings` set to OFF for org LUM-522.

maya: seeing immediate reduction in GPU queue length on pool-a. Token-level KV cache hits up slightly — good.

sre-shift-lead: can we also ensure the customer isn't on an automatic retry loop from their side? Harper, ask them to pause and retry slowly.

harper: messaged LumenBay: "Please pause export job + stop auto-retries for 15m while we stabilize. We'll coordinate rollback after we confirm backlog drain." They acked.

liam: pulling logs. Example error slice (via `logtail`):

```
2026-03-15T16:04:17Z ERROR gateway request_id=abc123 org=LUM-522 path=/v1/generate latency=6123ms upstream=timeout
2026-03-15T16:04:18Z WARN ratelimiter org=LUM-522 attempted=218 allowed=0
2026-03-15T16:05:03Z INFO serving pool-a queue_length=112 active_exec=48
```

maya: looks like the burst saturated pool-a's concurrency for that model family. Good call on disabling batch-embed.

liam: after throttle and toggle, we dropped active_exec from 48 -> 12 within 90s. Errors fell from 91% -> 6%.

opsbot: Incident summary update: severity=P1, affected_org=LUM-522, mitigations_applied=[qps-throttle, feature-toggle(batch-embeddings)], pages=on-call.

sre-shift-lead: Liam — can you open a temporary quota exception for support/dev traffic so our health checks still run? Use low QPS token so probes don't skew usage.

liam: doing: `rictl token update --token monitor-probe --org LUM-522 --qps 1`

opsbot: Token updated. monitor-probe QPS=1.

maya: monitoring dashboards look stable. Next step: check usage pattern — is this an accidental customer script or a malicious higher-frequency job? Any identifying user-agent?

liam: from request headers: `User-Agent: LumenExport/1.9 (+exporter)` and `X-Client-Job: export_20260315`. Appears to be internal scheduled job kicked off by their infra.

harper: customer confirms they kicked a full org export by mistake. They'd like a temporary quota increase to finish export faster once we allow. We should not lift until backlog drained and we confirm safe rate.

maya: agree. Proposed follow-up: keep throttles for 15m, then run a controlled ramp: increase to 60 rps with burst=120, monitor for 2m, then either continue ramp or revert. Documented rollback plan: immediate revert to 30 rps.

sre-shift-lead: please coordinate with billing/PS for any committed overage. Also capture an incident runbook entry for LumenBay.

liam: prepping controlled ramp. Will route traffic to pool-b (less busy model replica) if we need capacity. Command for ramp is: 

```
rictl org update --org-id LUM-522 --qps 60 --burst 120 --route pool-b --note "controlled ramp after mitigation"
```

maya: leaving watch on metrics. Harper, let customer know controlled ramp plan and we’ll confirm 2m stability before increment.

harper: messaged them, they appreciate the plan.

opsbot: Automated health check: after initial mitigation, platform-wide error-rate normalized within 2 minutes.

liam: executing controlled ramp to 60 rps at 16:10:18Z.

opsbot: Command executed by liam at 2026-03-15T16:10:18Z: `rictl org update --org-id LUM-522 --qps 60 --burst 120 --route pool-b`

maya: metrics look OK at 60 rps for 3 minutes. No gateway timeouts, GPU queue stable.

sre-shift-lead: good. Leave throttles at 60 for 20 minutes and monitor. Create postmortem ticket and label with customer impact: partial outage (429/503) for 7 minutes.

liam: created PM ticket: INC-2026-847-LUM-522. Harvester: assigned to maya + liam.

harper: customer requests timeline and root cause summary. I’ll prepare a brief for them once we have the postmortem draft.

maya: post-incident actions:
- confirm export job logic with customer (prevent full-org blasts)
- add per-org safety circuit to block >X concurrent long-running ops
- enhance admin console to show active long jobs for orgs
- add prominent CSR runbook for controlled ramps

sre-shift-lead: handoff: I’m taking nightwatch at 16:30Z. If anything degrades, escalate to oncall. Leave notes in the ticket.

liam: leaving a short checklist in the incident ticket with exact commands used and timestamps.

opsbot: Incident P1 resolved -> downgraded to P2 at 2026-03-15T16:30:20Z. Mitigations remain in place until PM follow-up.

harper: customer thanked us and paused their export until they apply a paginated/export-resume pattern.

maya: closing thread — will update postmortem later today with timeline and recommendations. Great run team. :thumbsup:
